nodes.label: Global Data Centre Energy Demand Landscape
nodes.description: AI-driven data centre power consumption is the fastest-growing sector within energy demand; Goldman Sachs forecasts 50% growth by 2027 and 165% by 2030; AI workloads expected to grow from 14% to 27% of global DC power by 2027; global DC consumption reached ~415 TWh in 2024, projected to reach 945 TWh by 2030 per IEA

attributes.growth_rate_cagr: 12% annually since 2017 (4x faster than total electricity consumption)
attributes.critical_constraint: Estimated 20% of planned DC projects could face delays due to grid constraints

nodes.norm_label: global data centre energy demand landscape

nodes.label: European Data Centre Market Transformation
nodes.description: FLAP-D (Frankfurt, London, Amsterdam, Paris, Dublin) hubs facing congestion at 33-42% of local electricity consumption; Nordic and Southern European markets emerging with uncongested grids; EMEA capacity totals 11.4 GW live with 26.2 GW pipeline (live + UC + planned); DC demand projected to grow from 96 TWh (2024) to 236 TWh (2035) — a 146% increase

attributes.market_shift: 50% of European DC capacity will be outside legacy FLAP-D hubs by 2035
attributes.connection_timeline_constraint: 7-10 years in legacy hubs; 1 year achievable with smarter agreements
attributes.renewable_advantage: Nordic/Southern Europe have 2x faster growth rate vs FLAP-D (+110% vs +55% by 2030)

nodes.label: UK Data Centre Market Strategic Importance
nodes.description: Third highest DC count globally (500+ facilities); electricity consumption forecast to grow from 5.0 TWh (2023) to 26.2 TWh (2030) — a 424% increase; ~2.9 GW IT capacity with 6.2 GW planned by 2030; 70% clustered in M25 region; AI data centres have more variable load profiles than traditional cloud DCs; grid connection queue exceeds 700 GW

attributes.constraint: Iver-B substation power availability delayed until 2030-2033; operators funding own grid connections

nodes.norm_label: uk data centre market strategic importance

nodes.label: Germany Data Centre Infrastructure Landscape (MaStR-Informed)
nodes.description: Germany is Europe's largest DC market with 490+ facilities and 4.26 GW IT load; Frankfurt dominates with 74.7% of national capacity but faces grid saturation at capacity limits with pro-rata allocation; Brandenburg/Berlin secondary market growing with 50Hertz TSO actively seeking anchor loads; wind capacity 88.83 GW (31,986 turbines), solar 93.5 GW; 554 registered large power consumers across states; 21 TWh DC consumption in 2024 (4% of gross power consumption)

attributes.frankfurt_constraint: Grid fully allocated with all new capacity subscribed; 5-10 connection requests/year all oversubscribed
attributes.secondary_growth: Brandenburg (43 registered consumers, 17.06 GW renewables) has best power-to-load ratio
attributes.regulatory_mandate: New DCs from 2026 must achieve PUE ≤1.2; existing DCs must reach PUE ≤1.5 by July 2027

nodes.label: Ireland Data Centre Policy Framework Reset (LEU Decision Dec 2025)
nodes.description: CRU moratorium (2021) re-opened via new Large Energy User (LEU) policy requiring dispatchable on-site generation/storage and 80% renewable PPA sourcing by 2030; Dublin remains Europe's second largest cluster with 1,150 MW operational (H1 2025) and 2,000+ MW pipeline; DC consumption reached 21.8% of Ireland's total metered electricity (6,969 GWh) in 2024, growing at 21.2% CAGR since 2015

attributes.policy_innovation: 6-year glide path with phased connection tranches based on grid upgrade timelines
attributes.flexibility_obligations: DCs must demonstrate demand response capability and grid ancillary service participation
attributes.grid_performance: Renewable share 38.4% (2025), wind curtailment 11.3%, Celtic Interconnector (700 MW, France-Ireland) due online 2027

nodes.norm_label: ireland data centre policy framework reset (leu decision dec 2025)

nodes.label: Nordic Region Data Centre Competitiveness (Norway, Sweden, Denmark)
nodes.description: Norway: 88% hydro + 13% wind generation (among Europe's cheapest/cleanest); DC demand tripling by 2030; OpenAI committed €1bn; free air cooling achieves PUE 1.1; NordLink/NSL interconnectors (1.4 GW each) link Norwegian prices to European markets; connection timelines 2-4 years. Sweden: DC demand tripling by 2030; Brookfield €9.3bn + Microsoft €3.2bn commitments; district heating integration mandated; PUEs 1.1-1.2 routine. Denmark: meta Odense hyperscale campus; 80%+ renewable electricity; Energinet ancillary services markets enable DCs to earn balancing revenues

attributes.free_cooling_advantage: Sub-zero winters; ambient temp advantage absent in Southern Europe
attributes.renewable_ppa_maturity: Well-developed green certificate systems and corporate PPA markets
attributes.grid_connection: 2-4 years typical (faster than FLAP-D or Germany)

nodes.norm_label: nordic region data centre competitiveness (norway, sweden, denmark)

nodes.label: Spain Data Centre & Renewable PPA Market Development
nodes.description: Spain has Europe's most developed corporate PPA market for wind and solar; PNIEC 2024 projects 46% electricity demand growth by 2030; installed renewable capacity: 30 GW wind, 28 GW solar PV, 2.3 GW CSP, 17 GW hydro; renewable share reached 57% in 2023, targeting 81% by 2030; Madrid (MAD) primary DC hub with growing alternative to FLAP-D positioning; long-term PPAs achievable at €35-55/MWh for large operators; AWS €15.7bn + Start Campus €8.5bn + Microsoft €2.1bn committed

attributes.cross_border_constraint: France-Spain interconnection only 2.8 GW (target 10% of capacity); structural weakness causing isolated price spikes
attributes.environmental_screening: ISA (Índice Sostenibilidad Ambiental) 0-4 classification determines wind/solar land eligibility for PPA development
attributes.cooling_challenge: Warm climate requires more active cooling (PUE 1.4-1.6); water stress risk in central Spain requires closed-loop cooling

nodes.norm_label: spain data centre & renewable ppa market development

nodes.label: Belgium Grid Stability: Nuclear Baseload + Offshore Wind Expansion
nodes.description: Belgium's nuclear provides ~50% of generation; Doel 4 and Tihange 3 life-extended to 2055; 2.3 GW offshore wind installed (Alpha, Beta, Gamma, etc.); Prinses Elisabethzone (PEZ) will add 3.5 GW by 2030, tripling offshore capacity; Google entry (2010) now powers >60% of Belgian total DC capacity, transforming market; Brussels metro primary cluster with Saint-Ghislain (Google 250 MW+), Zaventem, Gosselies locations; data centre grid connection timelines 3-7 years for HV (>30 MW)

attributes.hyperscale_transformation: Single operator can reshape regional DC ecosystem when anchoring sufficient load
attributes.offshore_wind_grid: Horta-Ventilus offshore wind grid and Borealis project will resolve Flanders bottleneck by 2030
attributes.ppa_market: PPAs typically 10-15 years at €45-65/MWh for large operators with offshore wind

nodes.norm_label: belgium grid stability: nuclear baseload + offshore wind expansion

nodes.label: Southeast Europe Data Centre Market Emergence
nodes.description: Athens standout hub with 101 MW operational (highest in SE Europe); Microsoft expanding with 3 sites + campus plans; subsea cable landing stations provide MENA connectivity advantage; Trans Adriatic Express (TAE) low-latency route through Crete-Sofia-Bucharest-Zagreb; Bucharest steady growth with Digital Realty/Microsoft activities; Zagreb wholesale colo focus via ALTUS IT acquisition; Sofia measured growth; tax incentives, land availability, lower costs, and MENA/Eastern European demand proximity driving investment

attributes.infrastructure_maturity: Less mature grid infrastructure vs Western Europe; higher regulatory complexity; smaller local talent pools
attributes.connectivity_advantage: Crete subsea cable hub positions SE Europe as alternative Mediterranean gateway to MENA
attributes.risk_profile: Regulatory complexity and supply chain fragmentation require deeper due diligence

nodes.norm_label: southeast europe data centre market emergence

nodes.label: Data Centre PUE Efficiency Plateau & Hardware Density Paradox
nodes.description: Average global PUE stagnated at 1.55-1.6 since 2013 despite improvements from 2.5 in 2007; premium facilities and new hyperscale DCs consistently achieve 1.1-1.3; efficiency gains in hardware (wider bandgap semiconductors, better power supplies) are being offset by increasing compute density and AI accelerator deployment; AI workloads generate more heat per unit of floor space, requiring more intensive cooling; water consumption for AI (ChatGPT ~500ml per 5-50 prompts vs Google Search ~0.5ml) increases 1,000× with AI

attributes.water_stress_correlation: High-density AI GPU racks have proportionally higher water footprint; SE England faces critical water stress (World Resources Institute Aqueduct)
attributes.cooling_costs: Cooling systems account for up to 40% of DC energy demands (range: 24% most efficient to 61% least efficient)

nodes.norm_label: data centre pue efficiency plateau & hardware density paradox

nodes.label: Hyperscaler Pre-Leasing and Build Strategy
nodes.description: Entire campuses now pre-leased before construction begins; space sold before construction commenced increased 33x since 2019; space sold under construction increased 2.8x; self-builds dominate in power-rich regions (Nordics, US Southeast); build-to-suit and modular design enable faster deployment in constrained markets; DC operators securing power and land 24-36 months before delivery in constrained regions; power access has become the single greatest determinant of delivery speed globally

attributes.market_signal: Hyperscalers willing to pay premium prices and lock capacity years in advance indicates structural undersupply
attributes.easing_approach: Partnership models between operators, utilities, and suppliers becoming standard
attributes.geographic_implication: Shift toward power-rich regions (Nordics, US Southeast, Southern Europe) with lower land costs

nodes.label: UK AI Growth Zones & Critical Infrastructure Classification
nodes.description: Data centres reclassified as Nationally Significant Infrastructure Projects (NSIP) in September 2024; AI Growth Zones launched June 2025 offering streamlined planning and access to significant power connections (500 MW+); Secretary of State overruled local DC rejections (90 MW Buckinghamshire, 96 MW Hertfordshire); this represents significant policy shift accelerating DC deployment timelines in UK market

attributes.planning_acceleration: NSIP status bypasses some local authority planning delays
attributes.power_allocation: AI Growth Zones offer direct access to grid capacity (500 MW+ individual projects)
attributes.policy_risk: Depends on continued government support; local opposition remains significant

nodes.norm_label: uk ai growth zones & critical infrastructure classification
